title: Sell Mineral Rights in Garner, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Garner, AR | White County
metaDescription: Own gas royalty rights near Garner, Arkansas? We evaluate White County Fayetteville Shale legacy interests and make a straightforward, no-obligation cash offer.
heroLead: Garner is a small White County town where Fayetteville Shale leasing reached nearly every family's land at some point, even where drilling activity stayed modest.
intro: If you own minerals near Garner, there's a good chance the interest traces back to a lease signed sometime between 2005 and 2010, when operators were working through this part of White County as fast as they could get landowners under contract. What happened after the lease was signed varies a lot from section to section, which is exactly why we check the specific well or lease history before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Boom-era leasing, uneven follow-through
paragraphs: The pace of leasing in this area during the Fayetteville Shale's peak didn't match the pace of drilling. Some Garner-area tracts ended up with producing wells, others didn't. Both outcomes are common enough that we don't assume either one without checking your specific legal description.

sections.heading: Decline behavior on the wells that were drilled
paragraphs: Where wells were drilled near Garner, they've generally followed the same pattern as the rest of the Fayetteville Shale: a strong initial rate followed by a steep decline over the first few years, then a long tail of low, slowly shrinking production. Current royalty checks reflect that tail, not the well's original output.
We price off current volumes and remaining decline curve, not off what an owner might remember from the well's early years.

sections.heading: Confirming your share of a family interest
paragraphs: Many interests here are split among heirs without a formal partition. We can work from a deed, a division order, or an old lease to confirm your specific fractional share through White County records.

faqs.question: How do I know if a well was actually drilled on our Garner-area land?
faqs.answer: Send us your legal description or deed and we'll check current operator and permit filings for that specific tract.

faqs.question: Our royalty checks have shrunk a lot since the well was first drilled. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's typical decline behavior for Fayetteville Shale wells, which drop off sharply after the first couple of years.

faqs.question: Can you buy just my share if I have several siblings who also own part of the interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can purchase individual fractional shares without requiring every heir to sell at the same time.

faqs.question: Can out-of-state heirs who inherited a share near Garner still sell remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly close with owners who live outside Arkansas. Documents can be handled by mail or electronically without requiring an in-person visit.
